_about: Each state's download, for .github/workflows/download.yml (and the restore steps in publish.yml, which check_site.py compares with this list). code: the data/<code> folder's name (nj covers nj and va); key: its cache's name; minutes: the download's time limit; run: the command.

states.name: New Jersey and Virginia
states.run: python3 states/nj/fetch.py; nj=$?; python3 states/va/fetch.py && exit $nj
states.note: v2: started fresh when the filled-in 2022-23 file went into git (states/nj/fill2022.py).

states.name: California
states.run: python3 states/ca/fetch.py

states.name: Texas
states.run: (command -v tesseract >/dev/null && command -v pdftotext >/dev/null || sudo apt-get install -y -qq poppler-utils tesseract-ocr >/dev/null); python3 states/tx/fetch.py
states.note: One file per bill; only changed files after the first copy.

states.run: python3 states/il/fetch.py

states.name: Indiana

states.run: python3 states/ar/fetch.py --votes && python3 states/ar/contacts.py 2023 && python3 states/ar/contacts.py 2024 && python3 states/ar/contacts.py 2025 && python3 states/ar/contacts.py

states.run: python3 states/ak/fetch.py && python3 states/ak/contacts.py 2023 && python3 states/ak/contacts.py

states.name: LegiScan states
states.run: python3 legiscan.py tn ok me ri vt dc && python3 states/tn/contacts.py 2023 && python3 states/tn/contacts.py && python3 states/ok/contacts.py && python3 states/me/contacts.py && python3 states/ri/contacts.py && python3 states/vt/contacts.py && ((command -v pdftotext >/dev/null || sudo apt-get install -y -qq poppler-utils >/dev/null); python3 states/me/laws.py --minutes 8 || true) && (python3 states/me/reports.py --minutes 6 || true) && (python3 states/ok/vetoes.py || true); (python3 states/dc/laws.py && python3 states/dc/contacts.py) || true
states.note: Tennessee, Oklahoma, Maine, Rhode Island, Vermont and the District of Columbia (since 2026-11-22) from LegiScan (LEGISCAN_API_KEY), in one job so they share one count of the month's queries (data/legiscan/usage.json; stops at 9,000 of the free 10,000). Then Maine's laws' signing dates and chapters (states/me/laws.py, at most 8 minutes a run) and its committees' divided reports' signers (states/me/reports.py, at most 6 minutes a run), Oklahoma's governor's yearly veto page (states/ok/vetoes.py, weekly), the District's acts and laws from the Council's law library on GitHub (states/dc/laws.py, daily) and its Councilmembers from dccouncil.gov (states/dc/contacts.py, daily).

states.note: The General Court's daily data files (current year), plus its public read-only SQL Server for past years (login read each time from the Legislature's own document, never stored).

states.name: Iowa
states.run: (command -v pdftotext >/dev/null || sudo apt-get install -y -qq poppler-utils >/dev/null) && python3 states/openstates_bulk.py ia && python3 states/ia/openstates.py && python3 states/ia/fetch.py && python3 states/ia/contacts.py
states.note: The first copy from Open States (2023-24 from its bulk file, states/ia/bulk.json; 2025-26 from the API, OPENSTATES_API_KEY, at most 100 requests a day), then legis.iowa.gov, a request every 6 seconds, for every bill that changed and, in the requests left, the official record of the rest; a run ends at once if the site's bot check appears (the owner's choice, 2026-11-13; on GitHub it appears after about 45 requests). contacts.py builds the contacts after it.

states.note: The first copy of 2024-26 from Open States' bulk files (states/fl/bulk.json), then flsenate.gov at its 10-second crawl delay for every bill that changed and, in the time left, the official record of the rest; a 429 means wait and try again (both houses' bills; /api/ is barred and not used), the House's member and committee pages; the first copy (about 17 hours) builds up over many runs; contacts.py builds the contacts after it.

states.name: New York
states.run: python3 states/ny/fetch.py
states.note: Everything New York's pages are built from (states/ny/fetch.py): the Senate's API (bills, only when it lists an update; prefiled bills in November and December of even years), and from nyassembly.gov (robots.txt bars only GPTBot) the Assembly memos, floor votes, committee agendas and, once a day, contacts. New York's files are at the top of data/ (data/ny holds the memos, the last-checked mark and problems.txt). Past sessions' bills_<year>.json.gz are in git. v1 started from the old ny-memos-v1 and ny-bills-v1 copies (download.yml's 'Start New York from its old copies').

states.name: Congress
states.run: python3 states/us/fetch.py --votes-minutes 30 && python3 states/us/contacts.py && (python3 states/us/meetings.py || true)
states.note: GovInfo's bill status zips (about 150 MB for three Congresses, read again when the server's copy is a week newer), the files changed since (from the sitemap), roll calls from the House Clerk and the Senate a second apart (the first copy, about 1,600, fills in over a run or two), and the congress-legislators member data; contacts.py builds the contacts after it; meetings.py reads the upcoming committee meetings from the Congress.gov API (it needs the CONGRESS_API_KEY secret, and is skipped without it).
